body: text seems to contain invalid UTF-8 which seems to indicate a bug elsewhere. Still we should tighten up the code by incrementing the column by the number of cells actually written by `grid_puts_len`, and not recalculating the `col` increment.
or actually not invalid utf-8, but `"  Qâ\u0089"` (where 89 is an unprintable control codepoint), which still looks like some kind of mojibake
Hi. Any news on this ? I'm getting this several time a day. I'd be willing to open a PR (if someone can point me in the right direction).

@yazgoo 
I think you would have to investigate yourself based on @bfredl's comments.  I guess it might be due to some truncation not taking into account multibyte characters somewhere.

@bfredl 
Maybe the `assert` there should only be done for `rdb=invalid` already?
But then it fails later:

> src/nvim/tui/tui.c:1306: tui_raw_line: Assertion `(size_t)attrs[c-startcol] < kv_size(data->attrs)' failed.

With that also deactivated the statusline and command line then looks like this with the test case:
```
 Qâ   ¡
(1 of 1):
```

@bfredl Could you please give a little more details so I can try and fix this ?
Thanks

Probably we should add a "visual NDEBUG" for release tarballs. In release mode

- unprintable unicode will be replaced by replacement char
- invalid attribute will be replaced with shiny red (indication of error, but does not stop you from using the editor)

But a master build should still enable all asserts by default (otherwise no one would report issues).
